value.text: VERDICT: FAIL - The note adds facts not in the email ("solvent" paint, a 53' dry van) and tells the operator to confirm the hazard class and packing group, which the email already gives (Class 3, PG II).

VERDICT: PASS - The note plainly states the order, explains it was held for possible hazmat with no UN number, matches the codes, and gives concrete next steps; extra details like "dry van 53'" are presumably system defaults rather than invented facts.

VERDICT: FAIL - The email only says it is a resend of LT-48810, yet the note states a shipper, pallet count, weight, equipment, locations and dates that do not appear in the email, so it appears to invent facts.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents facts the email never states, including "48' flatbed with tarps", the shipper name and address "Ridgeline Build (purchasing@ridgelinebuild.example)", and the year 2026, and it also tells the operator to confirm what is changing when the email says plainly that only the delivery date moves to 12/14.

The note says "a 53' dry van load" and names Lakeshore Home with an email address, but the email itself mentions neither the equipment nor the shipper's name. The sender identity may come from headers, but the equipment type is likely invented. That breaks the "invents no facts" requirement.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents a fact the email doesn't support (that order 55102 is a "53' dry van load"), even though it is otherwise actionable.

VERDICT: PASS - The note plainly states the request, explains that it is held for a missing or uncertain pallet count (matching the codes), and gives a clear next step, with no facts that clearly contradict the email.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note never says the shipper asked for "the Metro Grocers DC". It claims no facility could be identified, when the real problem is that two Metro Grocers DCs match. The operator is not told to choose between them, so the note misstates why the order was held.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note wrongly says the email has no lane or freight details, when it names Appleton→Atlanta and Appleton→Dallas, dry van, about 6 loads a week, and it never tells the operator those specifics of what was asked.
VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents details not in the email, such as "53' dry van" equipment and "solvent" paint, which breaks the no-invented-facts requirement.
VERDICT: FAIL - The note is clear and actionable, but it states a "53' dry van" that the email never mentions and misspells the shipper's name as "Caldervhem", so it adds unsupported details.

VERDICT: FAIL - The email body only says it is a resend, yet the note states specific shipper, commodity, weight, equipment, dates and locations that do not appear in the email shown, so they look invented.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents facts not in the email (a 48' flatbed with tarps, the year 2026, and likely the Ridgeline Build name and address), and it never plainly says the change is pushing delivery to 12/14 while pickup stays 12/10.
VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents a fact the email does not contain: it calls order 55102 "a 53' dry van load".

VERDICT: FAIL - The note says the pallet count was "not stated clearly enough to read" and tells the operator to reread the email, but the email gives no pallet count at all. It also never says the account requires one. That misstates why the order was held, and the 53' reefer detail does not appear in the email.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note never says the shipper named "the Metro Grocers DC" or that two Metro Grocers DCs could match, so it calls the facility missing when it is ambiguous and does not tell the operator exactly what to confirm.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents facts: it calls the trailer a "53'" dry van, though the email just says dry van. It also contradicts the email by saying there is no lane and that the van is the only detail, when the shipper named two lanes (Appleton–Atlanta, Appleton–Dallas) and about 6 loads a week each.
VERDICT: FAIL - The note is actionable and matches the codes, but it adds details the email never states, such as a "53' dry van" and "solvent" paint.

VERDICT: PASS - The note plainly states the requested order, explains the hazmat hold consistent with the codes, and gives clear next steps (confirm hazmat status, get UN number/class/packing group or SDS), though details like the 53' dry van are not in the email and are assumed to come from customer defaults.

VERDICT: FAIL - The email gives only "Resend: Load Tender LT-48810" and a one-line note, yet the operator note states shipper, pallet count, weight, equipment, locations and dates that appear nowhere in the email, so it seems to invent facts.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note adds details the email never gives (48' flatbed, tarps, the 2026 year) and never states the actual change requested, which is moving delivery to Monday 12/14 while pickup stays 12/10.
VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents a fact, that the order is a "53' dry van load", which appears nowhere in the email, even though it is otherwise clear and actionable.

VERDICT: PASS - The note states the order details, explains the hold on the missing or unclear pallet count in line with both codes, and gives the operator clear next steps. Details like the 53' reefer appear to come from account data rather than being invented.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note never says the shipper asked for "the Metro Grocers DC" or that two Metro Grocers DCs could match, so it misstates the ambiguity as an unidentified destination and leaves the operator without the specific question to ask.

VERDICT: FAIL - The note invents facts: it calls the equipment "53' dry van" when the email says only "dry van," and it claims there is "no lane" even though the email names Appleton→Atlanta and Appleton→Dallas.
